<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{thmMain}
Let $1<p<\infty$, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure
space and let
$T \in B(L^p(\Omega))$
be a positive strongly Kreiss bounded operator. Then there exist
constants $C,\kappa>0$, depending only on $p$ and $C_{SK}(T)$, such that
\begin{equation*}
\left\|T^N\right\|_{B(L^p(\Omega))}
\leq
C\bigl(\log(N+1)\bigr)^\kappa,
\qquad N\geq1.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lemKrivine}
Let $X$ be a Banach lattice, let $S:X\to X$ be positive and let
$1\leq r<\infty$. Then, for every finite family
$x_1,\ldots,x_m\in X$,
\begin{equation*}
\left(
\sum_{j=1}^m \left|Sx_j\right|^r
\right)^{1/r}
\leq
S\left(
\left(
\sum_{j=1}^m\left|x_j\right|^r
\right)^{1/r}
\right).
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lemStirling}
There exist constants $c_{exp}>0$ and $N_0\geq1$ such that, for every
integer $N\geq N_0$ and every integer $k$ satisfying
\[
N-4\sqrt N\leq k\leq N,
\]
one has
\begin{equation*}
\frac{N^k}{k!}
\geq
c_{exp}\frac{e^N}{\sqrt N}.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lemInitialLocal}
Let $1<p<\infty$ and let $T$ be a positive strongly Kreiss bounded
operator on $L^p(\Omega)$. Then there exists
$C_0>0$, depending only on $p$ and $C_{SK}(T)$, such that
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{N+2-2\sqrt N\leq n\leq N}
\left\|T^n x\right\|_p^p
\leq
C_0 N^{p/2}\left\|x\right\|_p^p
\end{equation*}
for all $N\geq1$ and $x\in L^p(\Omega)$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
By positivity, assume $x\geq 0$. Lemma \ref{lemStirling} yields $N^n/n! \geq c_{exp} e^N/\sqrt{N}$ for $N+2-2\sqrt{N}\leq n\leq N$ and $N$ sufficiently large. Since $x\geq 0$,
\[
|e^{NT}x|^p 
= \left( \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{N^n}{n!}T^n x \right)^p 
\geq \frac{c_{exp}^p e^{pN}}{N^{p/2}} \sum_{N+2-2\sqrt{N}\leq n\leq N} |T^n x|^p.
\]
Integrating and applying \eqref{eqSK} gives the desired result.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lemLocalGlobal}
Let $\alpha\geq0$ and $A>0$. Assume that
\begin{equation}\label{eqLocalGeneral}
\sum_{N+2-2\sqrt N\leq n\leq N}
\left\|T^n x\right\|_p^p
\leq
A N^\alpha\left\|x\right\|_p^p
\end{equation}
for every $N\geq1$ and every $x\in L^p(\Omega)$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eqGlobalGeneral}
\sum_{n=1}^N\left\|T^n x\right\|_p^p
\leq
2^{2\alpha+1} A
N^{\alpha+1/2}\left\|x\right\|_p^p
\end{equation}
for every $N\geq1$ and every $x\in L^p(\Omega)$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Let $M\geq1$. For every $1\leq k\leq M$, applying
\eqref{eqLocalGeneral} with $N=k^2$ yields
\[
\sum_{(k-1)^2+1\leq n\leq k^2}
\left\|T^n x\right\|_p^p
\leq
A k^{2\alpha}\left\|x\right\|_p^p,
\]
since $k^2+2-2k=(k-1)^2+1.$ Therefore
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{M^2}\left\|T^n x\right\|_p^p
\leq
A\sum_{k=1}^M k^{2\alpha}\left\|x\right\|_p^p
\leq
A M^{2\alpha+1}\left\|x\right\|_p^p.
\]
For arbitrary $N$, choose $M=\lceil\sqrt N\rceil$. Then
$N\leq M^2$ and $M\leq2\sqrt N$, which gives
\eqref{eqGlobalGeneral}.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{corInitialGlobal}
There exists $C>0$ such that
for every $N\geq1$ and every $x\in L^p(\Omega)$,
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{n=1}^N\left\|T^n x\right\|_p^p
\leq
CN^{(p+1)/2}\left\|x\right\|_p^p.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lemLifting}
If $T$ is strongly Kreiss bounded, then $\mathbf T$ satisfies
\begin{equation*}
\left\|e^{z\mathbf T}\right\|_{B(\mathcal X)} \leq C_{SK}(T)e^{\left|z\right|}, \qquad z\in\mathbb C.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{lemKrivine}, for every $k\geq0$,
\[
\left|(U^k\otimes T^k)F\right|_{\ell^p} 
= \left(\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}\left|T^k f_{j-k}\right|^p\right)^{1/p} \leq T^k\left|F\right|_{\ell^p}.
\]
Thus,
\[
\left|e^{z\mathbf T}F\right|_{\ell^p} 
\leq \sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{\left|z\right|^k}{k!} \left|(U^k\otimes T^k)F\right|_{\ell^p} 
\leq \sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{\left|z\right|^k}{k!} T^k\left|F\right|_{\ell^p} 
= e^{\left|z\right|T}\left|F\right|_{\ell^p}.
\]
Taking the $L^p$-norm and applying \eqref{eqFubini} and \eqref{eqSK} yields $\left\|e^{z\mathbf T}F\right\|_{\mathcal X} \leq C_{SK}(T)e^{\left|z\right|}\left\|F\right\|_{\mathcal X}$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lemBootstrap}
Suppose that $p>\beta>1$ and that there exists $A>0$ such that for every $N\geq1$ and every $x\in L^p(\Omega)$
\begin{equation}\label{eqHbeta}
\sum_{n=1}^N\left\|T^n x\right\|_p^p
\leq
A N^\beta\left\|x\right\|_p^p.
\end{equation}
Then there exists a constant $D_{p}>0$, depending only on
$p$ and $C_{SK}(T)$, such that for every $N\geq1$ and every $x\in L^p(\Omega)$
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{n=1}^N\left\|T^n x\right\|_p^p
\leq
D_{p}A
N^{(\beta+1)/2}\left\|x\right\|_p^p.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Let $x \in L^p(\Omega)$ and fix $N$ sufficiently large, set $m:=\left\lceil4\sqrt N\right\rceil$, and define $Y=(Y_j)_{j\in\mathbb Z}\in\mathcal X$ by
\[
Y_j
=
\begin{cases}
T^j x,&1\leq j\leq m,\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
By \eqref{eqHbeta},
\begin{equation*}
\left\|Y\right\|_{\mathcal X}^p = \sum_{j=1}^m\left\|T^j x\right\|_p^p \leq A m^\beta\left\|x\right\|_p^p \le 5^{p} A N^{\beta/2}\left\|x\right\|_p^p.
\end{equation*}
Let $W:=e^{N\mathbf T}Y$. By Lemma \ref{lemLifting},
\begin{equation}\label{eqWUpper}
\left\|W\right\|_{\mathcal X}^p \le 5^{p}C_{SK}(T)^p A e^{pN}N^{\beta/2}\left\|x\right\|_p^p.
\end{equation}
For an integer $n$ in the interval $N+2-2\sqrt N\leq n\leq N$, we have $W_n = \sum_{k\geq0} \frac{N^k}{k!}T^kY_{n-k}$. Whenever $1\leq n-k\leq m$, $T^kY_{n-k}=T^n x$, and therefore
\begin{equation}\label{eqCoordinateW}
W_n = T^n x \left(\sum_{\substack{k\geq0\\1\leq n-k\leq m}} \frac{N^k}{k!}\right).
\end{equation}
Let $K_N := \left\{ k\in\mathbb N_0: N-4\sqrt N\leq k\leq N-2\sqrt N \right\}$. For $N$ sufficiently large, if $N+2-2\sqrt N\leq n\leq N$ and $k\in K_N$, then $1\leq n-k\leq m$. Moreover, $|K_N| \ge \sqrt N$, and by Lemma \ref{lemStirling}, $\frac{N^k}{k!} \geq c_{exp}\frac{e^N}{\sqrt N}$ for $k\in K_N$. Consequently,
\[
\sum_{\substack{k\geq0\\1\leq n-k\leq m}} \frac{N^k}{k!} \geq \sum_{k\in K_N}\frac{N^k}{k!} \geq c_{exp}e^N.
\]
It follows from \eqref{eqCoordinateW} that $\left\|W_n\right\|_p \geq c_{exp}e^N\left\|T^n x\right\|_p$. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eqWLower}
\left\|W\right\|_{\mathcal X}^p \geq c_{exp}^pe^{pN} \sum_{N+2-2\sqrt N\leq n\leq N} \left\|T^n x\right\|_p^p.
\end{equation}
Combining \eqref{eqWUpper} and \eqref{eqWLower} yields $\sum_{N+2-2\sqrt N\leq n\leq N} \left\|T^n x\right\|_p^p \le 5^p\left( \frac{C_{SK}(T)}{c_{exp}}\right)^p A N^{\beta/2}\left\|x\right\|_p^p$. Applying Lemma \ref{lemLocalGlobal} with $\alpha=\beta/2$ gives
\[
\sum_{n=1}^N\left\|T^n x\right\|_p^p \le D_p A N^{(\beta+1)/2}\left\|x\right\|_p^p,
\]
with $D_p := 2^{p+1}5^p\left( \frac{C_{SK}(T)}{c_{exp}}\right)^p$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{propOrbit}
There exist constants $C_p,\kappa_p>0$, depending only on $p$ and
$C_{SK}(T)$, such that
\begin{equation}\label{eqOrbitFinal}
\sum_{n=1}^N\left\|T^n x\right\|_p^p
\leq
C_pN\bigl(\log(N+2)\bigr)^{\kappa_p}
\left\|x\right\|_p^p
\end{equation}
for every $N\geq1$ and $x\in L^p(\Omega)$.
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Let $N\ge 2$ and set $\beta_0:=\frac{p+1}{2}$ and $\beta_{j+1}:=\frac{\beta_j+1}{2}$, so that $\beta_j = 1+\frac{p-1}{2^{j+1}}$. Corollary \ref{corInitialGlobal} gives the desired estimate for $j=0$. Inspecting the constants in Lemma \ref{lemBootstrap} and Lemma \ref{lemLocalGlobal} yields the existence of $C>0$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eqIteration}
\sum_{n=1}^N\left\|T^n x\right\|_p^p \leq C D_p^j N^{1+\frac{p-1}{2^{j+1}}}\left\|x\right\|_p^p
\end{equation}
for every $j\geq0$ and $x \in L^p(\Omega)$. Choosing $j = \lfloor\log_2\log(N+1)\rfloor$ gives $2^j\leq\log(N+1)<2^{j+1}$, from which $N^{\frac{p-1}{2^{j+1}}} \leq e^{p-1}$ and $D_p^j \leq (\log(N+1))^{\log_2 D_p}$. Inserting these bounds into \eqref{eqIteration} yields \eqref{eqOrbitFinal}.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
The argument above is strongly lattice-theoretic. In particular,
Lemma \ref{lemKrivine} is valid on arbitrary Banach lattices and
does not depend on the particular representation of $L^p$.

The specifically $L^p$ ingredient is the exact identity
\[
\left\|
\left(\sum_j\left|x_j\right|^p\right)^{1/p}
\right\|_p^p
=
\sum_j\left\|x_j\right\|_p^p,
\]
which is used both in the lifting argument and in the bootstrap.
Thus the same proof extends, with the appropriate constants, to
Banach lattices for which the corresponding upper and lower
$\ell^r$-lattice estimates are simultaneously available, together
with the dual estimates on $X^*$.

It would be interesting to determine the optimal formulation of this
argument solely in terms of lattice convexity and concavity. This is
closely related to the framework of Deng, Lorist and Veraar
\cite[Section 4.1]{DLV}, who proved polynomial-logarithmic bounds for
positive strongly Kreiss bounded operators on $p$-convex and
$q$-concave Banach lattices.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
Theorem \ref{thmMain} answers
\cite[Question 5.8]{ArnoldCuny} affirmatively. It also implies that,
for a positive strongly Kreiss bounded operator on $L^p$,
the infimum of the exponents $\theta\geq0$ for which
\[
\left\|T^N\right\|=O(N^\theta)
\]
is equal to zero, thereby answering \cite[Problem 5.6]{DLV} at the
level of the polynomial scale.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
